hooks.text: A nearby planet completes its entire year in 18 hours.
One year on this nearby giant planet lasts only 18 hours.
This nearby planet is twice Earth's size but has 18-hour years.

title: The Extreme 18-Hour World of 55 Cancri e
description: Discover 55 Cancri e, an extreme super-Earth orbiting so close to its star that its year lasts only eighteen hours, featuring a magma ocean and a volatile atmosphere.

beats.text: A nearby planet completes its entire year in 18 hours.
beats.visual: artist concept of the exoplanet 55 Cancri e orbiting its host star, 2017

beats.text: Discovered in 2004, 55 Cancri e is a rocky super-Earth twice the size of our home world.
beats.visual: artist impression of a super-Earth exoplanet, 2021

beats.text: It orbits its sun-like star so closely that the planet is tidally locked in a permanent death spiral.
beats.visual: artist concept of a tidally locked planet orbiting close to its star, 2015

beats.text: The star-facing dayside roasts at over 2,000 Kelvin, a temperature hot enough to melt iron.
beats.visual: illustration of a lava-covered exoplanet dayside facing its host star, 2016

beats.text: In 2012, one controversial hypothesis suggested this carbon-rich world might have an interior of solid diamond.
beats.visual: artistic rendering of a diamond-rich exoplanet interior, 2012

beats.text: But in 2024, the James Webb Space Telescope detected a thick, volatile atmosphere on this hellscape.
beats.visual: illustration of the James Webb Space Telescope in deep space, 2021

beats.text: This atmosphere is likely outgassed from and sustained by a bubbling ocean of liquid magma.
beats.visual: close-up photograph of active bubbling lava lake in Ethiopia, 2018

beats.text: That molten surface races around its host star in just 18 hours.
beats.visual: artist concept of the planet 55 Cancri e, 2017

better_than_last: Ensured Beat 5 includes claim 1 and explicitly attributes the diamond theory as an early hypothesis to meet the research rules.
